title: Regions: isolation, compliance, and data residency
hook: An AWS Region is a separate geographic area with its own power, networking, and control plane. Data stays inside the Region you choose unless you explicitly replicate or read across Regions — that boundary is how compliance and data residency work on AWS.

blocks.text: A Region (for example ap-south-1 in Mumbai or eu-west-1 in Ireland) is a fully isolated partition of AWS. Each Region contains multiple Availability Zones. Services you create in a Region — Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances, Simple Storage Service (S3) buckets, Relational Database Service (RDS) databases — store primary data in that Region. Cross-Region access requires explicit configuration such as S3 Cross-Region Replication or reading from another Region API endpoint.

entries.plainDefinition: Geographically isolated AWS partition with its own Availability Zones and service endpoints.
entries.example: ap-south-1 serves workloads targeting Indian users and residency rules.

entries.plainDefinition: Policy that customer data must remain within a legal geography.
entries.example: Healthcare records processed only in an approved Region.

entries.plainDefinition: Region disabled by default until enabled in account settings.
entries.example: af-south-1 (Cape Town) requires opt-in before deployment.

entries.plainDefinition: Isolated cloud instance — aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov.
entries.example: Commercial aws partition Regions do not share data with aws-us-gov.

blocks.text: Wrong Region choice breaks compliance audits, adds latency for primary users, and blocks services not yet available in that Region. Regulators and enterprise customers ask where primary data lives — Region is the first answer.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: Region is the residency boundary. I pick Region for law, latency, and service availability — then design multi-AZ inside it.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Account selects a Region
items.body: Every API call targets a Region endpoint. Resources are Regional unless marked global (IAM, Route 53 public hosted zones).

items.title: Data stays local by default
items.body: S3 objects, EBS volumes, RDS storage remain in the Region unless replication rules move copies.

items.title: Cross-Region is explicit
items.body: Snapshots copied to another Region, Aurora Global Database, or S3 Cross-Region Replication — all opt-in with their own billing.

items.title: Compliance maps to Region
items.body: Certifications and features vary; verify before promising GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI scope in a given Region.

snippet.label: List enabled Regions for your account
snippet.explanation: Confirms which Regions are available before CloudFormation deploy. Opt-in Regions appear only after enablement.

snippet.label: Pin CLI commands to a Region
snippet.explanation: Every CLI call without --region uses the default. Production scripts should set region explicitly to avoid accidental cross-Region resources.

snippet.label: CloudFormation Region-scoped stack
snippet.code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Residency-aware bucket in ap-south-1
Resources:
  DataBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub "${AWS::AccountId}-in-residency-data"
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
snippet.explanation: Stack deploys into the Region where you run aws cloudformation deploy --region ap-south-1. Bucket data never leaves unless you add replication.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Picking us-east-1 by default without checking user latency or residency. Assuming all AWS services exist in every Region. Enabling cross-Region replication without legal review. Confusing global services (IAM) with Regional data stores (RDS).

interviewTakeaways: A Region is an isolated geographic partition — primary data stays there unless you configure cross-Region copies.
Choose Region for compliance, latency to users, and service availability before optimizing cost.
Use KMS keys in the same Region as encrypted data; audit ARNs in CloudTrail for cross-Region calls.
60s: Region = residency boundary. Multi-AZ inside Region for HA. Cross-Region replication is explicit and billable.
Follow-up: how do opt-in Regions and AWS Outposts change the residency story?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'AWS is global so data is everywhere' gets you rejected — Regions are isolated unless you replicate.
Strong answer: name the Region, cite residency requirement, then multi-AZ — not 'we use the cloud.'
Deploying to us-east-1 because tutorials use it while primary users sit in Mumbai.
Enabling S3 Cross-Region Replication without updating data processing agreements.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node.js Lambda sets AWS_REGION automatically. Browser apps never call AWS directly — wrong Region in backend env vars creates resources far from users, similar to pointing a C# app to the wrong connection string server.

TypeScript APIs often route tenants by Region header or subdomain (eu.app.com). Same pattern as choosing an AWS Region per tenant for residency — unlike a single on-prem SQL Server instance serving all tenants.
